data.description:
## Context / Problem

`gate_status(job_id)` reports a run as terminal (`status: "passed"`, with a `verdict`) before
that run's `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar is readable from the tickets tracker. The documented
poll-then-read workflow — start a gate with `review_plan_start`, poll `gate_status`, then read
the findings to remediate — therefore has a window in which the caller reads the PREVIOUS
run's findings and believes they are the ones just reported.

This is silent: nothing distinguishes a freshly-written sidecar from a stale one at read time,
so the caller acts on findings it has already addressed.

## Reproduction

Observed 2026-09-01 while remediating `responsive-undamaged-auklet` (`549b-9cc5-940e-46c3`).

1. `review_plan_start responsive-undamaged-auklet` returned
   `job_id 1788326596882647223-94573cf0d90d404e87c74855306c16f2`, whose id prefix places the
   start at 22:23:16.
2. After the run, `gate_status` on that job returned `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "BLOCK"` —
   polled twice, both terminal.
3. At that moment the newest sidecar under `.tickets-tracker/549b-9cc5-940e-46c3/` was
   `1788325963941841589-…-REVIEW_RESULT.json` (22:12:43), which belongs to the PRIOR run, and
   the directory held 6 sidecars for 6 completed runs minus one.
4. Reading "the latest findings" therefore returned the prior run's two findings verbatim.
5. Re-checked later: `1788327281362056852-…-REVIEW_RESULT.json` (22:34:41) was present, with
   the actual findings for that job, and the count reconciled.

Expected: once `gate_status` reports a terminal verdict for a job, that job's sidecar is
readable — or the response says the record is not yet durable. Actual: terminal status is
reported while the sidecar for that job is still absent.

The consequence is not hypothetical: in this session it produced a remediation pass aimed at
findings that had already been fixed, and only a timestamp comparison between the job id and
the sidecar filename revealed the mismatch.

## Scope

The gate-run status surface and its relationship to sidecar durability:
`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py` (the run index that `gate_status` replays) and the plan-review
sidecar write path. Either the terminal transition waits on the sidecar write, or
`gate_status` exposes whether this job's sidecar is readable yet.

Note `gate_status` already carries a `durable` block for the signed ATTESTATION. That block
reports attestation currency, not sidecar readability, and on a BLOCK verdict it is
`unsigned` by definition — so it cannot be used to distinguish "findings ready" from
"findings not yet written".

## Non-goals

- Changing when a verdict is computed, or the verdict itself.
- Making sidecar recording non-best-effort in a way that would fail a run whose findings
  failed to persist; the verdict must still be reported.
- The `plan_review_status` / attestation currency semantics.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive if solved by exposing readability on the status response; behavior-narrowing if
solved by deferring the terminal transition until the sidecar lands. Either way no stored
event shape changes and back-out is reverting the status surface. Existing callers that
ignore the new field keep working.

## Testing

Unit tests against the real run-index replay with a stubbed sidecar writer, driving the
window explicitly: assert the status contract holds while the sidecar is absent and after it
lands. The race is made deterministic by controlling the writer rather than by timing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a job whose verdict is recorded but whose sidecar has not been written,
      `gate_status` does not present that job as having readable findings — either it is not
      yet terminal, or the response carries an explicit not-yet-readable indicator; verified
      by `pytest` with a stubbed writer held open, asserting the returned fields.
- [ ] Once the sidecar for that job is written, `gate_status` reports terminal AND readable,
      and the sidecar whose event id corresponds to that job is the newest for the ticket;
      verified by `pytest` asserting both after releasing the stubbed writer.
- [ ] A caller following the documented poll-then-read sequence never observes a prior run's
      findings as the current job's; verified by `pytest` driving two successive runs over a
      seeded store and asserting the findings read after each poll belong to that run's id.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; the documented poll-then-read sequence
cannot return a prior run's findings for a job reported terminal.
data.title: gate_status reports a terminal verdict before its REVIEW_RESULT sidecar is readable
